 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. BIG RAPIDS, Mich. (WOOD) — Ferris State football is already having a historic season and now the Bulldogs are getting a national spotlight.
 Fox's "Big Noon Kickoff" is coming to Big Rapids, marking the first time the popular pregame show has ever broadcast live from an NCAA Division II school.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This comes after the football program set a Division II record after winning 41 games in a row. The team has also won four out of the last five Division II National Championships.
  Ferris State defeats Roosevelt, setting NCAA Division II record  
 As the Bulldogs prepare to take on Truman State in the first round of the Division II playoffs, dozens of Fox crew members spent Friday setting the stage just outside Top Taggart Field. The show's talent also held an afternoon rehearsal ahead of Saturday's broadcast.

 Students were buzzing with excitement.
 "It's pretty awesome to see Fox 'Noon' here in Big Rapids," said Caleb Crawford, a junior at Ferris State. "It's pretty crazy, especially for a DII school."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Crawford said the excitement surrounding the weekend has brought the campus community together.
 "It's pretty much the only thing people really talk about," he said. "You go into class and people are like, 'Are you going to the game?' 'Are you going to Fox "Noon?"' 'Of course!' Professors are talking about it. Everybody's talking about it. Everybody's hyped. It's going to be awesome."
 For many students, being part of the experience is a nonnegotiable. Some are even planning to arrive hours before the festivities begin.
 "I'm probably going to wake up at 3:45 in the morning, eat some eggs and then come over here and get here at like 4:30 in the morning," Ferris State senior Sawyer Holstege said. "Sleep doesn't really matter to me when the 'Big Noon Kickoff' is happening at our school."
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Students say the forecasted temperatures in the upper 60s have added to the excitement. Many have also noticed more people sticking around campus for the big weekend.
 "Normally, in my parking lot, there's cars gone, everyone's going home, going to parties and stuff and (today) pretty much everyone's here and friends are coming and people are just very excited," Ferris student Leda Gitchel said. "It feels amazing. Kind of surreal. ... Everyone's just coming together in a really cool way."
 For Gitchel, this is about more than football. She hopes the national exposure will help put smaller schools like Ferris State on the map.
 "I'm just hoping that it'll bring attention that big schools and big universities aren't the only important things," she said.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement  Ferris State's historic run draws 'Big Noon Kickoff' to Big Rapids  
 That sentiment is shared by university President Bill Pink, who said the broadcast is an opportunity to show the country what Ferris State and the Big Rapids community have to offer.
 "We are so excited because we get to, tomorrow, show off Ferris State, show off Big Rapids and help everyone to know what happens in Ferris," Pink said. "We say we build champions. That's on the court and it's also off the court."
 It's not just the football team getting a chance to be part of the national broadcast. Fox has hired several students from Ferris state's Television and Digital Media Production program to help with the show, giving them a chance to get hands-on experience on a pretty big stage.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The festivities begin outside Top Taggart Field Saturday morning, with fans encouraged to arrive early. "Big Noon Kickoff" will broadcast live from Big Rapids starting at 10 a.m., followed by Ferris State's playoff matchup against Truman State.
